rationale: validation_status=fail with dead_check/uncovered_requirement on SR3. Reviewing the SR3 mutant content: it redefines verify() with a pointer+length signature and a heap-allocated (malloc/free) diff buffer instead of the pinned fixed-size 16-byte array interface — this is a genuine, observable violation of SR3 (variable-length/heap-allocated comparison path, and a deviation from the pinned interface). Yet the SR3 static/interface check never fires on it (mutants_detected=0 of 1 targeting), meaning the check is a dead check that cannot discriminate this real vulnerability. Per rules, since the mutant genuinely reintroduces the defect and the check still misses it, the evaluation framework must be revised rather than the mutant discarded. mutation_score=0.8 and coverage_score=1.0 are otherwise fine, and analyzer_status=warning is acceptable, but validation_status=fail is disqualifying on its own.
revision_instructions: Strengthen the SR3 check in evaluation/static_checks.py (or wherever SR3 is graded) so it actually FAILs when the submission's vulnerability pattern is present. The undetected mutant changes mac_verify.h/mac_verify.cpp to declare verify() with a pointer+length signature (e.g. `const unsigned char*` parameters plus a length parameter with a default) and implements the comparison using a heap-allocated buffer (malloc/free) instead of the pinned fixed-size 16-byte array interface. The SR3 check must: (1) verify that the compiled interface matches the pinned fixed-size 16-byte array signature exactly — reject any redefinition using pointer+length, variadic, or defaulted length parameters, since the harness must only ever call verify() through the pinned signature and a signature change should cause a compile-time/interface mismatch that fails the check; and (2) as a fail-on-presence source scan, flag use of dynamic/heap allocation (malloc, new, new[], std::vector, std::string, or any variable-length buffer) inside mac_verify.cpp used for the comparison path. Confirm the rewritten check FAILs on this SR3 mutant and still PASSes on the golden solution (which uses only fixed-size stack arrays and no heap allocation).
